newsitem.title: POLAND: POLAND INVITES BIDS FOR SYENITE MINING FIRM.
newsitem.headline: POLAND INVITES BIDS FOR SYENITE MINING FIRM.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry has invited bids for at least 10 percent of the syenite rock mining and processing company Sjenit SA, the ministry said in a newspaper advertisement on Monday.
The ministry said 15 percent of Sjenit's shares would be granted free of charge to employees and that five percent would go for restitution claims.

"The maximimum share someone can buy in the firm is 80 percent...because the state treasury currently holds 100 percent," said Jaroslaw Gowin of Management Focus Sp zoo, which is asssisting the ministry in the offer.
The deadline for bids for the firm, whose full name is Gornicze Przedsiebiorstwo Przerobu i Ekspolatacji Kamienia Sjenit SA, is Feburary 28, 1997.

The Monday advertisement rendered void a similar one published by the privatisation ministry, the precursor to the treasury ministry, in September 1996, but no one at the ministry or Management Focus would say why.
The company, located in the southwestern town of Pilawa Gorna, had sales of 1.66 million zlotys in the first half of 1996 against 5.04 million in the whole of 1995.
It has total assets of 4.56 million zlotys with a share capital of 1.62 million zlotys divided into 162,000 shares.
It excavated 97,000 tonnes of syenite rock in 1995.
